title: Frontend: Social Share
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Social Share. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({adapter=success,url=https://example.test/article}). Share uses an injected asynchronous adapter: success resolves to Shared, cancel to Cancelled, missing/reject to Copy link instead. Show [data-testid=status] and readonly Link input only for fallback. This tests UI adapter outcomes, not native OS sharing.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Invoke the Web Share API from a user gesture when supported and fall back to a copyable URL or explicit provider links.
alternativeApproaches: Add file sharing using capability checks without assuming every browser accepts the same file types.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Native support missing; user cancels; URL with reserved characters.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
